title: Cop justified in shooting 63-year-old: Special Investigations Unit
article: A Toronto officer was "legally justified" in shooting a 63-year-old man last month during a confrontation with police resulting in the man's death, the province's Special Investigations Unit said Friday.
Antonio Bellon was shot dead after police were called to a laneway in northwest Toronto on Jan. 10 to investigate a threatening complaint.
Sgt. Allen Jenkins, who was shot in the arm after being called to help on the scene, suffered an injured shoulder.

Officers responded to the Saturday night call by attempting to speak to Bellon, following him through a narrow pathway near his home, said a release by the unit, a civilian agency that reports to the Ontario attorney general's department.

The unit said that Bellon was armed with a shotgun and fired it at Jenkins, hitting him in the shoulder. Jenkins then ordered Bellon to put the firearm down, and when Bellon didn't respond, Jenkins fired three shots at him.
A post-mortem concluded Bellon died from a gunshot wound to the chest. Jenkins underwent surgery in hospital shortly after the shooting.
After investigating, unit director John Sutherland concluded "there was only one course of action open to the officer, and he took it."
